legal.definitions: Anti-snagging rule (WAC 220-300-160(2)): except when fishing a buoyant lure with no added weight, or trolling from a vessel or floating device, terminal gear is one lure or bait with one single-point hook. Night closure (WAC 220-300-160(22)): closed to fishing from one hour after official sunset to one hour before official sunrise. Adult salmon (WAC 220-300-010): Chinook over 24 in, coho over 20 in, chum over 12 in.

structure.what: A straightened section with little instream large wood, plus mainstem and side-channel habitat. For over 100 years, bridge crossings for Auburn-Lake Holm Road (with the rail line) have held the floodplain to about a third of its historic width and kept the channel along the north valley wall
A large log jam downstream at RM 32.5 (King County). Its position relative to the stands is not mapped here

A buried rock revetment beneath the site access road that forms the western edge of the largest wetland. Removal is planned with a Summer 2028 construction target, so it is still there now. Where it meets the river is not mapped

Fenster: City of Auburn and King County removed about 700 linear ft of the old Fenster Levee and set it back (2006-2009). The work removed the rock armor, buried and anchored 60+ logs with rootwads along the toe of the bank, created 5 instream pools, and reconnected an old side channel. Pautzke Slough off-channel habitat is just upstream

Far bank: King County says Green River Community College and the Washington DNR own the right (north) bank in this reach, with an access trail from the college to that bank. OSM puts the campus polygon about 0.78 km NE of the stand and the 'Oxbow at Green River College' stream about 190 m NNE (bearing 35)

OSM maps a cluster of buildings about 445-465 m NNW, across the river (bearing 310-350, inside your forward view), outside the mapped college campus. What they are, and whether they show through the trees, is NOT proven

The SR 18 mainline is about 0.6 km SSW of the stand (bearing 201, behind-left). The two SR 18 river spans are about 0.97 km ESE (bearing 102, behind-right). King County says the Hwy 18 bridge affects the channel about 1,500 ft upstream and downstream. Whether the road or bridges are visible from the bank is NOT proven

The BNSF Stampede Subdivision rail line runs about 340 m south of the stand (bearing 191). Houses along SE Auburn-Black Diamond Rd are about 390-420 m south. Both are behind you, and their visibility is unproven
